subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: Should OpenClaw accept a scoped native-Linux VPS reasoning-latency runbook as core docs/instrumentation work, and what minimum trace set counts as done?
rationale: The request is valid and aligned with performance priorities, but the acceptable measurement environment, trace scope, and whether this belongs as docs-only analysis or code instrumentation are maintainer product choices.

options.title: Scope a core runbook
options.body: Define the native Linux host profile, required trace fields, quick-win config guidance, and follow-up split criteria before queuing implementation work.

options.title: Defer to narrower performance issues
options.body: Keep this issue as an umbrella reference while asking reporters to use specific existing issues for event-loop, bundle-tools, auth, memory, and Telegram bottlenecks.

options.title: Close as support after guidance
options.body: Treat the report as environment-specific support and point users to existing diagnostics docs without adding a dedicated VPS reasoning-latency artifact.

recommendation.title: Scope a core runbook
recommendation.body: Define the native Linux host profile, required trace fields, quick-win config guidance, and follow-up split criteria before queuing implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: The history search shows the broadest recent ownership across the affected runtime, docs, diagnostics, and memory surfaces.
